evidence: Screenshot Img5.png shows the mixed render. MAY ALREADY BE FIXED: commit 911fd92 (2026-08-13) is titled 'the app ran in Ukrainian under an EN label'. The screenshot's provenance relative to that commit is unknown — re-verify against HEAD before dispatching a fix. If it still reproduces, it is a regression and needs a test, not just a fix.
fix_hint: Depends on re-verification. If it reproduces, the EN dictionary is missing these keys and the resolver falls through to uk instead of to English.
notes: 2026-08-19: Not a resolver bug and not fixed by 911fd92, which addressed the lying badge, not the dictionary. Mechanism confirmed: uk HAS dashboard.nextJobTitle / nextJobNone / moneyInFlightTitle / moneyHeld / moneyCleared (the exact Cyrillic strings in Img5) and LACKS keys for 'This week' / 'Today' / 'Rating' / 'Good evening', which fall back to English. 911fd92's own message says 'Ukrainian has 468 keys; the app uses more, so the rest fell back to English.' uk is marked status:'ready' in i18n-locales.js and offered in the picker, which violates the policy written at the top of that same file: 'a half-translated locale offered in the picker is worse than one that is not.' Compounded by SB-0008 — the badge said EN, so the user could not tell they were pinned to uk.
repro: Open the business Dashboard with the language badge reading EN. Section headers render as 'НАСТУПНА РОБОТА', 'Немає запланованих робіт', 'переказано вам', 'ГРОШІ В РУСІ', 'На депонуванні', 'Переказано', while 'Good evening', 'THIS WEEK', 'TODAY', 'RATING' and the tab bar stay English.
title: Business dashboard renders Ukrainian strings in an English session
verify: Fresh install, set language to English, open the business Dashboard, assert no Cyrillic renders. Add a jest test asserting translations.en has a key for every key translations.uk defines on the dashboard.

evidence: Screenshot Img6.png. The badge and the sheet disagree, so a user cannot tell what language they are actually in — which is the mechanism behind Img5's mixed dashboard. Same fix-commit caveat as the dashboard finding: 911fd92 claims this exact symptom was fixed on 2026-08-13. SettingsScreen.js:54 carries the comment 'the app rendered Ukrainian. Subscribe instead of snapshotting.'
fix_hint: the chip reads UK for Ukrainian, AR for Arabic, EN for English, FR for French — always matching the checkmark in the sheet, and still matching after force-quitting and relaunching the app
notes: 2026-08-19: 911fd92 fixed HALF of this. It made the badge subscribe (onLocaleChange, SettingsScreen.js:56) so the value is no longer a stale snapshot — but the badge's FORMATTER is still a two-way ternary: SettingsScreen.js:296 'currentLocale === fr-CA ? FR : EN'. i18n-locales.js offers FOUR status:ready locales (en, fr-CA, ar, uk), so uk and ar both fall to the else branch and render 'EN'. Structurally incapable of showing the truth. Preview build post-dates the fix (97c146c Aug 15 > 911fd92 Aug 13), and no commit has touched i18n.js or SettingsScreen.js since — so HEAD is the fixed version and the symptom survives it.

2026-08-19: Root cause was the FORMATTER, not the staleness 911fd92 fixed. SettingsScreen.js:296 was 'currentLocale === fr-CA ? FR : EN' against four ready locales. Replaced with localeChipLabel() derived from the LOCALES registry, so a locale promoted to 'ready' can never again be added to the picker and forgotten in the chip. Verified the new guard FAILS on the old line and passes on the new. On-device confirmation queued in the phone retest pass.
repro: Settings -> Language. Set Ukrainian, back out to Settings, read the chip on the Language row. Then set Arabic and read it again. Then English.
title: Language badge reads EN while Ukrainian is the checked selection
verify: cd mobile && npx jest src/__tests__/locale-chip-tells-the-truth.test.js -w 2 — 6 tests, incl. a call-site guard that fails if SettingsScreen re-hardcodes the ternary. Device confirmation: Settings chip must read UK when Ukrainian is checked.
